yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point and every list item is there, in order, with the edit and all four example sentences. Additions hang off the original: "sounds like yer grandad", "as fake as a three-dollar note", and an expansion of the order note, "Sheilas first for the posh one, blokes first for the casual one." which is correct. The frame "So a bloke wanders in with an answer." makes the answerer male, a small invention.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "no bugger ever whinged" for no one complained, "takin' the piss" for mockery, "she'll be right" for likely to be fine, "cop a funny look" for a strange reaction. "coves" for men is dated but carries the sense. "sheilas" for women fits the voice, though in a text about which gendered terms might offend, it is itself a loaded choice.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly sounds like a real Aussie: "doin' me head in", "got the old noggin tickin'", "boring as", "quick smart", "brand-spankin'-new ute". A couple of lines lean stock: "as fake as a three-dollar note" and "coves", which no one under eighty says.
yarn-troppo.register: A full yarn at level 5: "Righto, here's one that's been doin' me head in", "Then it fair knocked me flat". Swearing stays within level 2: "bloody well should", "takin' the piss".
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps the earnest, slightly fussy asker and the helpful answerer: "Hope I haven't knocked out every bloody option -- got any ideas, anyone?" The added jokes ("like a bloke leanin' on the bar") lift it a touch past the original's mildness but do not invert it.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads well aloud: "Say this, and no one's gonna get their back up:". A few joins are busy, e.g. "Try this on a couple of girls and they'll be wary of ya quick smart, and fair enough too:".
yarn-troppo.variety: Plenty of different colour, but "sheila" is leaned on hard: "blokes 'n sheilas, even a room full of just sheilas", "so I've heard from sheilas", "You'll even hear sheilas call other sheilas", "a couple of sheilas".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the forum question and answer, with its two lists of rejected words and the gals examples, retold: "So what's a sheila's version of 'guys', or one with no gender in it at all?"

engine.meaning: Swaps the very word under discussion, so the text stops making sense: "Strewth, what's a feminine version of 'blokes'?", "What might be a female gendered or non-gendered version of 'coves', cobber?", "“Blokes” can be used in English as gender neutral", and "“Coves and gals” is a rather informal variant of “sheilas and gentlemen.”" The list also changes "everyone, youse" and "(as much as 'young fellas')".
engine.sense: Many terms take the wrong sense because they replace mentioned words: "'blokes'" and "'coves'" for the word guys, "“sheilas and gentlemen.”" for ladies and gentlemen, "gals, mate." inside the quoted word. "ya drongo" turns a polite request into an insult.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: interjections bolted onto unchanged sentences, "Stone the crows, so, some that I wouldn't consider", "Crikey, I realised", "Fuckin' hell, Edit:", "Fair fuckin' dinkum, but if yer explaining". US forms left: "patronizing", "truck".
engine.register: Most of the body is the original word for word ("It's colloquial but not rude, off puttin', condescending, patronizing"), with tags stuck on, so it is well short of a level-5 yarn; the swearing ("Fuckin' hell") is within level 2 but bolted on.
engine.tone: The mild, considerate tone is wrecked by "any suggestions, ya drongo?" and "Fuckin' hell, Edit:", which make a polite asker abusive and an edit note angry.
engine.flow: Jarring joins and broken grammar: "Fuckin' hell, Edit: As noted by", "Stone the crows, so, some that", "So anyway, it’s not likely".
engine.variety: A string of different stock exclamations ("Strewth", "Crikey", "Stone the crows"), but they are all the same move, a tag at the start of a sentence, repeated.
engine.essence: The shape of the post is there, but a question about the word guys that never asks about guys is barely the same text: "What might be a female gendered or non-gendered version of 'coves', cobber?"

unharnessed.meaning: Every point, list item and example is there and accurate: "Nobody ever whinged about it, to my face or behind my back", "(Note it's back to front.)". "they might reckon you're dodgy as fuck" renders might make them doubt you, a fair colour.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "up itself" for condescending, "a drama" for a problem, "taking the piss" for mockery, "get anyone's back up" for offend, "switched the light on" for sparked realisation.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, plain Australian, nothing stock: "rock up to a couple of women", "just casual like", "bloody well should". It leaves US "grocery store" and "truck" in the examples, though those are quotes from the original.
unharnessed.register: Lighter than a level-5 yarn: much stays near the original wording, "So what'd be a female version of 'guys', or one with no gender at all?", "Any ideas?". One swear within level 2: "dodgy as fuck".
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the earnest, considerate voice of both asker and answerer: "Hopefully I haven't knocked out every option. Any ideas?" The one swear is in a jokey aside and doesn't change the mood.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Then it hit me I'd also been using it for any mob of people, blokes and sheilas, even just sheilas on their own."
unharnessed.variety: Varied and light, nothing leaned on; "mob" appears twice and "sheilas" a few times, but it mixes in "women".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original: both lists, the gals pairing and the four examples, "Alright, guys on this side of the room, gals on the other."
